title: Wood v. Northwest Georgia Presbytery
disposition_detail: Complaint declared judicially out of order under OMSJC 10.5.c because Northwest Georgia Presbytery rescinded the action complained against; dismissed because the defects could not be cured and no grounds remained. No merits determination. Dissent would have found the complaint judicially in order and directed panel adjudication.
first_summary: Laura Wood’s complaint against Northwest Georgia Presbytery was dismissed as judicially out of order because Presbytery rescinded the action complained of, leaving no grounds. The SJC reached no merits. A dissent argued the complaint should have proceeded.
summary: A complaint challenging Northwest Georgia Presbytery’s denial of Laura Wood’s complaint against a session was declared judicially out of order and dismissed because Presbytery later rescinded the challenged action; the SJC said the defects could not be cured and no grounds remained. It reached no merits. The dissent argued rescission did not automatically defeat a complaint and that her complaint also alleged Presbytery’s failure to act.

sources.supports: Adopted majority judgment, rescission rationale, dismissal, roll call, and separate dissent.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: Case 2010-24, Wood v. Northwest Georgia Presbytery, before the SJC of the 40th GA (2012). The opinion by RE John White was adopted, as amended, as the full SJC decision; vote was 16 concurring, 6 dissenting, 1 recused, 1 absent (lines 1-3, 25-31; printed pp. 525-526).
evidence_notes.dispute: Wood complained to the SJC after Northwest Georgia Presbytery acted on her earlier complaint against the Session of Grace Covenant PCA; the dissent records Presbytery’s September 11, 2010, negative answer to Complaint #2 and its January 29, 2011, rescission (lines 13-21, 71-74, 97-118; printed pp. 525, 527-529).
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: The SJC held the case judicially out of order under OMSJC 10.5.c because Presbytery had rescinded the action complained against; it said the defects could not be cured and dismissed because no grounds remained (lines 13-22; printed pp. 525-526). The dissent, not the adopted decision, argued rescission did not automatically make the complaint out of order and that a failure-to-act specification remained (lines 40-60, 88-122; printed pp. 526-530).
evidence_notes.qualifications: The majority made no merits determination. The dissent expressly expressed no view on the merits and rested on the asserted invalidity of the out-of-order ruling and the continuing failure-to-act claim (lines 40-44, 120-130; printed pp. 526, 529-530). TE McGowan’s recusal explanation appears separately (lines 33-36; printed p. 526).
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: No incorporated decision is supplied; the majority refers to OMSJC 10.5.c and BCO 43-8, but those texts are not reproduced in the source (lines 13-21, 48-52; printed pp. 525, 527).

source_limits: The source contains the brief adopted majority opinion, roll call, and dissenting opinion, but not the full complaint, Presbytery minutes beyond quoted excerpts, or the cited OMSJC/BCO provisions. The record therefore supports the procedural disposition but not a merits assessment.
benchmark_examples: C01: preserve both procedural rulings and refused relief; here the adopted decision grants no merits relief and dismisses on procedural grounds.
C20: do not supply an explanation absent from the adopted ruling; here the majority did state a rescission-based reason, while the dissent’s contrary rationale remains separate.

score_reasons.concrete_dispute: The synopsis identifies the challenged Presbytery action and the complaint context without dwelling on names or filing chronology.
score_reasons.decision: It states the sole material outcome: judicially out of order and dismissed, with no merits ruling.
score_reasons.decisive_reason: It accurately gives the adopted reason: Presbytery’s rescission removed the grounds for the complaint and left defects incurable.
score_reasons.distinctive_value: It preserves the procedural distinction that rescission of the challenged action can produce an out-of-order dismissal, while noting the dissent’s contrary view.
score_reasons.fidelity: It distinguishes the adopted majority holding from the separate dissent and does not convert dissent arguments into the SJC’s decision.
score_reasons.economy: Every retained detail explains the dispute, the dismissal, or the limiting procedural reason.
